name: Waxed
process: Wax is rubbed into the sanded wood, left to harden and buffed; coats are renewed rather than stripped, so an old waxed surface builds a soft, deep polish, dirtier in the pores. Two traditions: European paste wax (beeswax, sometimes with carnauba, softened in a solvent), rubbed on cold; and the Chinese hot-waxing of hardwoods (烫蜡), in which the wax is melted into warmed wood and the surplus scraped and rubbed off. Historic Versailles parquet was waxed; Chenghuai's phoebe is waxed, never painted.

beeswaxComposition.text: Hydrocarbons 14 %, monoesters 35 %, diesters 14 %, triesters 3 %, hydroxy monoesters 4 %, hydroxy polyesters 8 %, acid esters 1 %, acid polyesters 2 %, free fatty acids 12 %, free fatty alcohols 1 %, unidentified 6 %.

versailles.text: Panels were assembled by hand without glue, then waxed.
versailles.source: Marc Maison, 'Parquet de Versailles', Architectural antiques resources, https://www.marcmaison.fr/architectural-antiques-resources/parquet-de-versailles (read 2026-09-26)

mechanism.text: As any clear finish near the cell wall's index: bare wood's surface scatter is removed and the fibre highlight appears.
mechanism.source: Marschner, S.R., Westin, S.H., Arbree, A. & Moon, J.T. (2005) Measuring and modeling the appearance of finished wood. ACM Transactions on Graphics 24(3), 727-734, https://doi.org/10.1145/1073204.1073254 (https://www.cs.cornell.edu/~srm/publications/SG05-wood-lr.pdf)

optics.surface: A thin, soft film that polishes where rubbed and stays dull in hollows and pores.

photograph: A buttery satin polish on edges and tops, duller in carving and pores; dust and wax dark in the pores and quirks.
On phoebe, the golden thread strongest on waxed curved surfaces.

unverified.reason: The method described is the trade's; no source describing 烫蜡 could be opened.
Beeswax about 1.443-1.449 (CRC as quoted by MFA CAMEO); page not opened.
